title: Enfortumab vedotin + pembrolizumab
context_label: First-line unresectable or metastatic urothelial cancer
indication_text: First-line unresectable/metastatic urothelial cancer in adults eligible for platinum chemotherapy.
purpose: Help control advanced urothelial cancer using a targeted chemotherapy-carrying antibody and immune treatment.
schedule_label: Confirm21-day or42-day pembrolizumab plan · EV days 1/8 in each21-day block
schedule_summary: Option 1: enfortumab on days 1 and8 plus pembrolizumab200 mg on day 1, repeating every 21 days. Option 2: enfortumab on days 1,8,22 and29 plus pembrolizumab400 mg on day 1, repeating every 42 days. Your team selects one option. The six-week reference shows two enfortumab blocks; pembrolizumab day 22 applies only to option 1.
administration_text: Enfortumab is given first over 30 minutes; pembrolizumab follows over 30 minutes when both are due. Enfortumab starts at 1.25 mg/kg with a125 mg cap. Staff confirm your current dose and chosen pembrolizumab interval; pembrolizumab is not dose-reduced for toxicity.

HbA1c, lipase, cortisol, nerve and eye reviews depend on symptoms and the plan. For the42-day option, the team must explicitly confirm tests for each enfortumab block.
safety_note: Follow your own prescription and hospital instructions. This information supports a discussion; it does not authorise treatment.
urgent_extra: Call oncology immediately for fever, shaking chills, suddenly feeling unwell, unusual bleeding, new breathlessness, very little urine, severe rash or vomiting that prevents drinking. Follow your hospital’s temperature and contact instructions. Severe breathing difficulty, chest pain, collapse or seizures: call 112/999.

agents.name: Enfortumab vedotin
agents.mechanism: Delivers a cell-division inhibitor to cells bearing nectin-4
agents.explanation: An antibody attaches to a protein called nectin-4 and delivers a chemotherapy payload that disrupts cell division. Healthy skin, nerves and other tissues can also be affected. This is not a checkpoint immunotherapy medicine.
agents.watch: Report any rash early, especially blistering, fever or mouth/eye/genital sores; also report thirst, frequent urination, numbness or new breathing symptoms.
risks: Skin rash, sometimes severe or life-threatening including Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis; serious reactions may occur in the first cycle
High blood glucose and diabetic ketoacidosis, including in people without known diabetes
Numbness, tingling or weakness from peripheral neuropathy, sometimes lasting
Dry eyes, blurred vision and corneal problems
Lung inflammation, sometimes severe or fatal
Low blood counts, serious infection, anaemia and bleeding
Fatigue, reduced appetite, taste changes, nausea, diarrhoea and hair loss
Infusion reactions and tissue injury from leakage outside the vein; fertility and pregnancy harm

agents.name: Pembrolizumab
agents.explanation: PD-1 is a control switch on T cells, a type of immune cell. When it connects with PD-L1 or PD-L2, the T cell receives a signal to reduce its activity. Some cancers use this pathway to escape immune attack. Pembrolizumab is an antibody that blocks PD-1, helping T cells recognise and attack the cancer. It does not directly poison cancer cells like chemotherapy. Releasing this brake can also allow immune cells to attack healthy organs, which explains the different side-effect pattern and why symptoms can appear after treatment stops.
agents.watch: The immune system can also inflame healthy organs. New cough, diarrhoea, unusual weakness, severe headache, thirst or a spreading rash need prompt advice. Effects can start during treatment or after it finishes.
risks: Immune inflammation of lungs, bowel, liver, kidneys, glands, skin and other organs
Effects can develop after treatment ends

anatomy: Report rash early. Blisters, peeling, mouth sores or fever with rash require urgent assessment.
Report tingling, numbness, weakness or difficulty walking early.
New cough or breathlessness may be lung inflammation; seek urgent advice.
Report new diarrhoea, blood in stool or abdominal pain; do not assume it is a routine side effect.
Blood tests check inflammation. Report jaundice or dark urine.
Report reduced urine, dizziness, severe weakness or persistent headache.
Thirst, frequent urine, vomiting or drowsiness may indicate dangerously high glucose.
Report visual changes. Immune inflammation can affect almost any organ, including heart, nerves and muscles.

evidence.title: EV-302 randomised phase III study
evidence.summary: In886 previously untreated patients, median overall survival was 31.5 months with the combination versus 16.1 months with platinum/gemcitabine (hazard ratio0.47;95% confidence interval0.38–0.58). Median progression-free survival was 12.5 versus 6.3 months.
evidence.intro: In886 previously untreated patients, median overall survival was 31.5 months with the combination versus 16.1 months with platinum/gemcitabine (hazard ratio0.47;95% confidence interval0.38–0.58). Median progression-free survival was 12.5 versus 6.3 months.
evidence.caveat: These are results from the primary analysis, not a personal prognosis or a comparison with every possible treatment sequence. The current NCCP indication specifies eligibility for platinum-containing chemotherapy.
evidence.interpretation: These are results from the primary analysis, not a personal prognosis or a comparison with every possible treatment sequence. The current NCCP indication specifies eligibility for platinum-containing chemotherapy.

questions.q: Does a delay mean treatment has failed?
questions.a: No. Blood counts, organ function and symptoms can make a delay or dose change safer. Your team decides whether and when to give the next dose.

questions.q: Who do I contact if unwell?
questions.a: Use your verified oncology daytime or out-of-hours number. If you cannot reach the team, seek urgent medical assessment. Severe symptoms require 112/999.
